name: Burgruine Ehrenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Ehrenberg Castle ruins near Reutte tower as a 13th-century hilltop stronghold, standing as the historic centrepiece of the Burgenwelt ensemble.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Ehrenberg Castle ruins (Burgruine Ehrenberg) near Reutte form the dramatic medieval core of the four-part Ehrenberg fortress system. Constructed around 1290 by Count Meinhard II of Tyrol upon a prominent rocky crag at nearly 1,100 metres above sea level, the stronghold served as an impregnable northern bulwark. Over the centuries, its massive ramparts, battlements, artillery bastions, and towers withstood fierce sieges, peasant revolts, and conflicts during the Schmalkaldic War. Although decommissioned in the late 18th century, decades of painstaking preservation have stabilised and restored the monumental stonework. Today, Ehrenberg offers an atmospheric encounter with high-medieval fortification architecture paired with breathtaking alpine vistas over the Lechtal and Allgäu Alps.

Route & Requirements

The walk up to the castle ruins is a rewarding, moderately graded trail suitable for visitors of all generations. From the valley visitor centre at the Klause, a well-marked forest trail climbs gently to the inner bailey in approximately twenty-five to thirty minutes. Alternatively, the modern Ehrenberg Liner funicular offers step-free access close to the castle portal. Sturdy walking shoes are recommended for exploring the historic flagstones, parapets, and bastion ruins. Explanatory signs installed across the site detail the former roles of the great hall, chapel, gatehouses, and artillery bastions.

Visiting & Getting There

The castle ruins are located directly south of Reutte along the B179 Fernpass route. Spacious parking facilities are provided in the valley basin. Regular regional buses connect Reutte in Tirol railway station to the 'Klause' bus stop. The castle ruins are freely open to the public daily year-round with no admission charge. Tickets are only required for the inclined lift or if you wish to cross the adjacent highline179 suspension bridge.

Tips

Directly beside the castle walls stands the entrance to the famous highline179 pedestrian suspension bridge, spanning across the valley in breathtaking fashion. Visiting during dusk is particularly enchanting when subtle floodlights illuminate the centuries-old battlements above the dark forest canopy. Ambitious hikers can continue upward from Ehrenberg to explore the higher-altitude baroque fortress ruins of Schlosskopf.
preis: Free of charge; Ehrenberg Liner inclined elevator optional extra
oeffnungszeiten: Freely accessible year-round (exercise caution in winter during frosty conditions)
